atoms.b: ((--The --A --An ++ )) Animals live in very different places: in ((++the --a --an --)) air, in ((++the --a --an --)) water, underground or on ((the a an ++)) land. You can find them everywhere, even in very hot places like ((++the --a --an -- )) desert or in very cold places like the North and South Poles. ((++The --A --An --)) animals that live in these extreme ((the a an ++)) conditions have adapted perfectly to them. ((--The --A ++An --)) adaption can mean that some parts of the body are smaller or bigger, depending on the conditions.

((++The --A --An --)) arctic fox, for example, has ((--the --a --an ++)) very small ears and ((--the ++a an --)) short tail. Smaller ears and tail means there is less space to lose body heat, so ((++the --a --an -- )) fox stays warmer. ((++The A An )) desert fox, on the other hand, has ((--the ++a --an)) longer tail, less fur and bigger ((--the --a --an ++)) ears.
